question: If an arc of \(45^\circ\) on circle \(A\) has the same length as an arc of \(30^\circ\) on circle \(B,\) then the ratio of the area of circle \(A\) to the area of circle \(B\) is
solution:
An arc occupies the same fraction of a circle's circumference as its degree measure occupies of \(360^\circ\). Let \(r_A>0\) and \(r_B>0\) be the radii of the two circles. Equal arc lengths give
\[
\frac{45}{360}\cdot2\pi r_A
=
\frac{30}{360}\cdot2\pi r_B.
\]
Canceling the common factor gives \(45r_A=30r_B\), so
\[
\frac{r_A}{r_B}=\frac23.
\]
Because a circle's area is \(\pi r^2\), the requested ratio is
\[
\frac{\pi r_A^2}{\pi r_B^2}
=\left(\frac23\right)^2
=\boxed{\frac49},
\]
choice A.
